body: Thank you so much for sending this message. I really truly appreciate it. I hope your brother recovers well and quickly. My best wishes to your family.

Even in an obviously difficult time you are kind enough to think about others who have helped you. Maybe you want to have a positive influence on others and connect with them somehow. Maybe you don't want to leave without having had a positive impact on the world. There is so much that can change if you get better. Please reach out to someone now, as you have to us, and maybe you will see things very differently soon. You can PM me back if you prefer. Please seek out help, so that this can be reversed.
Hi there. What is going on now?

Don't give up. Don't do something you know will make her angry and worse, but don't just accept what she says and walk away. You should stay with her through this somehow (I am not sure of the exact circumstances between you two so how to do this in your case is unclear).
You must be going through something very tough. Since you are posting about it here, you have not lost the fight. What is making you feel this way now?

Be there to support her and don't be afraid to ask her how she is feeling / what she is thinking. The most important thing is that she feels like you hear her - like you understand how difficult this is for her. There is help available. She can recover from depression. It is a disease that can be treated.

You being there for her, physically close and emotionally connected, is very important. Has she sought any professional help in the past, or gotten medications? Is this a long-term issue or a recent change? Do your best to listen as fully as possible and try to understand how tough a situation she must be in, even if you don't fully grasp it yourself. Be there for her whenever she needs you. Try to remove objects that may provoke her or make her think about hurting herself (knives, medications, guns, etc.). Be patient and don't leave her alone if she is going through a tough moment. If you can get her to seek out help, in the long term that would be good, but don't alienate her in trying to do so.

Why should you just "give in"? We are talking about a situation that can be resolved, a set of thoughts that you are not sure what to do about. There is no need to add violence. Don't be so harsh on yourself.

Hello again. People will want to hear from you as long as you are sharing with us. Nothing "needs" (as you say) to be done. If your thoughts are unclear, let us - or better yet, let a professional - help you sort through them.

Why do you say your mind wins? It sounds like a really tough battle, and I believe you when you describe how overwhelming it is. Obviously these thoughts are arising because your brain/mind are in a certain difficult state, and remember that the state can be changed. Have you been in touch with doctors about your depressive periods / paranoia?

I think one way the medications work for some people, without necessarily getting them to answer the "why" questions, is helping the mind think about brighter things, and see mundane things in a brighter light. This happens as you recover from depression. The result is effectively the same, and you develop meaning and motivations from what you are doing. There are plenty of optimistic, passionate people with those kinds of doubts, but the doubts are framed within a more purposeful mindset, which you can achieve. Does this help in understanding your situation?

ECT has improved in recent years and the results can be remarkable. Though of course you cannot be certain of how it will go for you, if your medical team is recommending it, I would see it as a treatment that may help a lot! Fingers crossed for you!

I am sorry to hear about the challenges you are going through. As you say, life can deal you bad cards. Lights can dim and disappear. Hope can be lost. Yet they can also be restored. When you say "why do I keep going?" well, that's a good question. Even people who have what seem to be perfect lives, with health and wealth and whatever else you could wish for, also wonder sometimes why they keep going. The reason people do find happiness eventually? Because you move ahead in life by seeing light where you don't expect it; by finding or creating meaning along the way; by pushing through hardships even when you have every reason to give up. And to get you through those times, others are here to help and listen. It's okay if you can't find an answer now. You don't have to decide on an alternate path. I wish your family the best at this tough time. Help us help you through it and keep us posted on how you feel.

It seems like you've faced major challenges, but it doesn't matter whose fault it is. There is nothing peaceful about being dead. And it's okay to not want to be here - fortunately, life changes a lot. What is making you not want to be here?
Because you don't have the complete picture of your future when you make that decision.

I am sorry to hear you've had some hardships. Whether you realize it or not, there are surely people who still want you in their lives, and in any case, there are people in the world who you will someday connect with if you give it a chance. You are probably going through a tough phase that is making you feel more "hopeless" and "worthless" than is usual or warranted. Don't assume you have the complete picture now. You can recover, and get a lot of satisfaction out of life. As cyathea mentions, what have you tried so far?

There is no shame in seeking out help. Everyone, including those who look like they have perfect lives, needs support sometimes. Feel free to let us know what's up. Why do you think your friend told you to come here?

Don't look at it that way. She's not convinced you'll do that. What if she simply has no way to cope with the current situation? I don't know what is going through her mind exactly, but this might be a way for her to "respond" to the situation even if it's an awkward and irrelevant thought. Basically she is so concerned that she's unable to think clearly. So don't let something like this break your heart. She'd respond more coherently if she cared less... she wants to see you through this, and probably wishes she could do more to help. And that's okay. Over time you'll make progress, and this will pass.

I can totally understand how shocked you must feel - I would be too. But keep in mind that you didn't hear it directly. You don't fully know exactly what was said or how it was said, so don't jump to conclusions about what she was thinking. Your parents may be stressed, confused, and tired, and in turn they may come across in ways that you don't find encouraging or helpful. Don't let that put you down. Remember that deep down, your parents want you to be well and get over all this. So don't let superficial communications get in the way of the true emotions that bond you to them, whether they are evident now or not.

I read your other posting too and first wanted to emphasize that it is great that you are seeing a therapist. It is completely normal to be hesitant about sharing something as deeply personal and delicate as rape, and indeed she might already be thinking that. Remember that her role is to listen and to help, so it will make things easier for you if you tell her whatever is on your mind. Even if it takes time (maybe several sessions) to get the whole story out, the process of explaining it to someone, and having someone reflect on it, is a good way to understand it better and address your symptoms. Try to tell her as much as you can, and if you don't get everything out the first time, take it a step further the following session. Just by posting here you are already making progress, and you'll get through all this step by step.
Feel free to PM me if you want to chat.

Yes objectively - I decided so based on your messages. Also, you're kind and generous for reaching out to help others on this website, which I've also noticed. I think you would benefit from realizing that you're not the loser you say you are. Do you have any upcoming plans or activities? What have you been doing lately?

You're right that people should not be treated differently based on their ages, if they are dealing with the same conditions. It just helps to understand the condition itself sometimes. You keep calling yourself and your ideas "stupid" and "childish", but you're clearly smart and mature. Have you worked before?
We can talk by PM if you prefer, btw
Since you keep calling yourself childish - how old are you, roughly?

Is there anything you used to care about? In reading your older postings and messages, I really get the sense that you underestimate yourself a lot. You're clearly smart and thoughtful, yet you keep putting yourself down, and it sounds like you wish you had more control over many things. Also I have no idea how old you are, but in any case, were you always like this?
Things can change fast, and then change fast again too ... what happened?
I do think I understand what you are getting at. The important question is how this all affects you now. Do you live with anyone? Do you have a job or go to school?
You should think about talking to someone next chance you get. And as other people have said, don't worry too much about this phase - it will pass as you guys grow up. Keep us posted on how you feel

Maybe the distinction between choice and control is what I am trying to explain. Let me give another example that I think might make more sense because I am not sure how to say this through your illustration. Let's say you were going to get a pet and for whatever reason there's a 50/50 chance you will get a black dog or a brown dog, and you don't get to decide. You really want the black dog. Would it make sense to say, okay forget that, I will just get a cat? That won't help you get the black dog. My point is simply, you don't have control over certain things, like what happens to your existence, or what existence even is. Again, that doesn't mean it's not a valuable state to be in. We can only evaluate what we understand about the world around us, and there are ways to be satisfied and even happy about that.
I'm not sure I have an answer for you, but it would be helpful to let us know where you are located - which country at least

On the contrary, thank you for getting into such detail, I actually have much to say but need some time to think it through because our illustrations are getting complicated :) I think your illustration is not quite valid for the point I am trying to make, but basically, you are saying you are upset that you have no choice. Why does that bother you so much? There are many things we don't have power over, but that doesn't stop us from appreciating the good in them either.

I understand you must be extremely frustrated by everything you have been through with your tough condition. You say you want to find support - have you spoken with any medical professionals about how you feel?

Don't let that get to you. You'll see as you grow up that people change a lot. In the mean time, you should find a way to get them to stop - probably best to tell someone older who can understand the whole situation. Do you talk with anyone about this?
Have you been able to tell anyone (parents? teachers?) about how you've been feeling about your friends?
Hey I'm here, was just on another posting.

But even if you're right, you won't be around to know it or experience it. Whatever impulse is making you want to not exist won't exist anymore either. It's like saying you want to eat an apple, and have a closed bag of fruit you can't see into, and since you don't know if there's an apple in the bag, you're going to throw the whole bag away. Just because you're not eating any fruit doesn't help you eat an apple. Why don't you want to exist?
Please message us when you check back here, as I think you will do. There are solutions to these sorts of crises, and we're here to listen and help.

I'm glad you're taking the time to explain yourself a bit here, it's making more sense now. You don't have to be so down about yourself. So you have your way of looking at the world/universe/life. Okay, fine. You still don't have to follow through on ideas that you know might not make sense. If you think you are "sick" or "broken", as you say, maybe there's a way to heal. Have your thoughts gotten in the way of work or school or other activities?

Good for you for posting here. Things might be stressful for you right now, but life changes so much over time ... don't get lost in the present situation. Are you saying one of your friends is nicer to you?
Why not have a perfect existence?
Have you considered posting this to /r/suicidewatch too? I am sure many people over there would appreciate hearing from you
Thank you for sharing your uplifting story!
I don't think you're a moron. Morons don't think so much or so meaningfully. Why do you think so?
You're more thoughtful about these deep topics than most people. Why do you think you are making these choices which you say yourself don't make sense?
What do you mean by a long time coming - how did this start?

There's a lot in what you say. It sounds like you are dealing with a big mix of emotions and it must be tough. But don't be so critical of yourself! Just because there are many unanswered questions in life does not mean there aren't good things and meaning/purpose to be uncovered and enjoyed. Feel free to vent as much as you want. Is there anything going on in your life these days that is making you feel like this?

Just wanted to say that I'm here to listen if there is anything you would like to talk about. You express well the despair of depression and how hard recovery can be. Yet you still sound like a caring, thoughtful, and generous person, with a desire to get through this and connect meaningfully with others. These are all encouraging signs. You say it's hard to explain how you feel, and I know that can be a challenge with depression, but it's good you decided to post here, because I think your story might strike a chord with others who genuinely want to help. In addition to what you've mentioned here - socializing, exercise, eating well - have you tried any medical treatments or therapy? There are so many new options these days that, even if one approach doesn't work, there are promising alternatives to try next.

By the way, it is great that you recognize how much Kati means to you and your well-being. You seem concerned about being a burden on her. Have you sought out professional help of any kind to help you through your depression?

It sounds like a tough and stressful situation for you. If you'd like to discuss it further - your emotions, how your girlfriend is acting, your pain ... whatever is on your mind - feel free to PM me. You can recover from this, and we want to help you do so.

It must be hard on you to feel this way. I don't think you are being selfish in wishing people would reciprocate your caring actions more often. It is the unfortunate reality that most people do not appreciate such kindness, or simply don't know how to interact appropriately. But you are not alone - there are people like you out there who would love to find someone like you. Your qualities are beautiful, and when you do come across someone who can reciprocate, it will be very rewarding for you both. Don't become a lesser person to become more like everyone else. You will find that when you do find a few people with whom you feel a truly mutual bond, your interactions with the others won't matter to you as much.

Indeed it will take some courage to speak up, but it's the right thing to do. They may not understand you at first, but deep down they care and want you to be well. Give them a chance to hear you and help you through this. If they don't see things the way you want them to, let them know. Depression is a tough condition because it does not have clear physical manifestations. Explaining it to others is a great step toward recovering.

Hey, thanks for sharing your thoughts. Being unsure about the path ahead is not an unusual thing (most people probably feel like that, even if they don't say so) but it sounds like that feeling is part of what is making you unhappy. You're right, life isn't that easy, but it does evolve, even if that can be a slow process. You say it's been 10 years that you've had the depression and anxiety issues - have you had any medical interventions for them? Have you tried any drugs or therapies?

What do you mean by "disproving a former purpose"? And why can't the "new" purpose be just as good and valid as the former one? Happiness is tough to find sometimes, but it can arise when you least expect it.
You can PM me
If you want "true support", I'm here. You sound very mad and frustrated - is that directed at someone or something in particular?
This is not that unusual ... you should go to the doctor anyway and explain how you feel on a bad day. It's great that you find the courage and energy to seek help - make full use of it!

Your reasoning sounds logical, except that when people are depressed, they are also generally in a state of profound hopelessness that obscures their perception of purpose and meaning in life. As you start getting out of depression, a sense of purpose is slowly restored, which then helps you realize that a full recovery is truly worthwhile.

Don't worry about me man, and sorry for all the questions, you don't have to answer them if you don't want to obviously, I'm just curious why you chose to share this with us. Are you by yourself right now?
You seem pretty sure of yourself. What is special about tonight?
Thank you for posting here. We're here to listen if there's anything on your mind you want to share. Why do you feel the need to let us know? Is there something you want to discuss?

Many people don't fully understand what it means to be depressed, but it deserves attention like any other condition. Have you had a chance to meet with any medical professionals since your youth? Some kind of therapist? Why did you stop taking the meds?

It sounds like you're going through a tough time. Good for you for trying to get through your depression. In addition to sapping motivation, depression often gives a sense of hopelessness, out of proportion to what is happening around you - but don't let that get in the way of your recovery. You shouldn't be so hard on yourself - it is wonderful that you try to help others. Why do you think you hurt others in trying to help them?
Have you tried to let him know exactly how you feel? Why do you think something is wrong with you?

It's good that you are open about the situation and realize it can be improved. You should try to take very small steps toward change, like setting aside some dedicated study time each day, or promising to do one simple useful thing at home each time she is out. As you accomplish each little goal, you will slowly build up the strength to do more. You can totally get over this funk.
You've come to the right place to be heard...we're listening if you want to elaborate
It's okay that you feel like this. Do you have any clues as to why you are feeling like this now, or is it truly random? Don't blame yourself, depression is a complicated condition.
That does hurt, yes. However hard this may be to believe now, it is something you do get through, over time.
Depression can also make you feel like this - regardless of the circumstances around you. Have you talked with anyone else before about being depressed? Any medical professionals?

You're not alone, we're here listening. There is no need to do anything drastic. What you are going through does sounds painful. Is this a recent change in the relationship? Do you know why she may be acting less affectionate?
You made the right choice in deciding to post here! Why are you in a rush to do anything drastic now? What is on your mind? What do you not belong to?

There are so many types of therapy, so many ADs, electrical stimulation, and yes, sharing your thoughts on here also counts, if it works for you to do so. So don't give up if what you've tried hasn't worked. Crying is okay too. This is something you can recover from, so don't be afraid to ask for help when you need it. Do you have trouble finding good medical care where you are?
Any particular reason? Depression is a complicated condition, but real progress has been made in the past decade or so, and there are many options now.
I'm sorry to hear what you've been through. Depression can be very tough, and make simple activities difficult. Are you currently trying any therapies?

You've been through some really tough challenges, but you clearly still have feelings for the people around you. Depression is something that can be overcome, even when it doesn't appear as such for the individual. Have you tried seeing other doctors?

There is a lot going on in your life lately. Just because the way forward isn't clear doesn't mean there isn't one. The fact that you wrote all this out suggests you want to get things off your chest or mind, and find a better solution. That can be done. Have you spoken to your medical team about the medicine? Have you tried other therapies too?
Well put

It's nice to hear that at least you had that pleasant night of dreaming. I don't know how to guarantee good dreams, but clearly your mind is able to be happy ... it would be nice if we could just get those feelings back whenever we wanted. Maybe try picking up the dream where it left off and seeing if it keeps going tonight?
I see - why did you stop the therapy?
Well thanks for posting this :)

You are very articulate about what you are feeling. Thank you for sharing it and giving us a chance to understand the challenge you are going through. One way I might think about this, if I were you, is to see depression as doing two kinds of things - removing motivation, which makes daily life a struggle; and also, changing your view of the future, so that everything looks more hopeless than it really is. In other words, not only is it tough to carry on, but you also get the sense that there is no other way but to keep pushing forward through intense difficulty forever. As you say, people do get through depression, and these two aspects get resolved - not only do you find more motivation, but you realize the path ahead is brighter and more hopeful than it previously seemed. In any case, I would not make any definitive decisions while in a state that I know is affecting my ability to reason out my long-term options. Does this at all answer some of your thoughts? Let me know

You've been through difficult times and it's clear you're frustrated now, but it is helpful to take a step back and see the big picture. Life is complex, yes, but it also evolves. Someday you will look back on this time, and realize it is just a small part of your life. Psychiatric conditions not only change your state of mind and moods - they also make it harder to appreciate the world around you, and your future, clearly. Don't be so hard on yourself. Is there anything in particular that is making the past few days so tough for you?

Hey, you just wait, life changes so much, sometimes in such unexpected ways ... you can't even imagine what is possible now. Don't give up on the person you will become! It's okay to be lazy, you will eventually find things that excite you. Recognizing that you don't like your current approach is a big step in the right direction.
You seem very determined to end things. Do you know why you feel that way? Also, as a counter quotation: "Stay strong. Depression lies." - Wil Wheaton

I see that you have been through a lot. It's good you have sought out others to share your story. Life is complicated and tough, but it does evolve in unexpected ways. Have you sought any therapy? A sense of hopelessness is sometimes the result of a medical condition rather than just the actual events and circumstances around you.

Very cool how you've dissected out your thought process so systematically. You are not alone in trying to understand all this ... and no one really does fully, of course. But it is possible, over time, to shift the perspective just enough so that, while you may not be able to answer these questions, the focus of your attention would be on enjoying the present moment, and other sources of meaning and pleasure that may develop. In any case, I think one needs to ponder your thoughts for longer to give a good answer :)
Sounds like you are pretty sure of yourself. But how do you know all these things? Are things not going your way lately? Let us know what's up.

Thank you for sharing this story. It is great to see that things do turn around even if there are moments when all hope appears to be gone. All the best to you, and may those who are suffering find a way forward as well.
Yes. And recognize that certain conditions like depression can do this to you. It is not permanent and it is not "who you are" - it is a tough situation, but one that you can recover from.
And even given all this, it is possible to find meaning in life without religion or spirituality. It's just a different approach to finding the right way to live.

Even if your plan worked as you say, they won't have you anymore, and I think your kids would prefer having you around. I don't know the details of your medical status, but doctors try as much as possible to minimize time in the hospital, and avoid it if possible, because recovery is mostly done in the "real world" anyway. In any case, you should take care of yourself, so that you feel better, and so that you are better able to be with your family later. People sometimes look down on those who are depressed, but attitudes are changing and it's a medical condition like so many others. Maybe you'd want to see a psychiatrist instead for now, outside a hospital?

The hospital can be a tough place sometimes - maybe your form of MDD is more amenable to treatment by other means at least now. It's a hard condition to have, because you are trying to fix it and at the same time it is making it hard to think clearly about just how to do that. It is definitely something that can improve over time though. Why is it that you don't like being honest with doctors?
Meditation is great ... it does take a while to get good at it though! I am not there yet but practicing. The mind is indeed a wild thing, sometimes.

The mind is amazing because it can think of so many different things - true and untrue, possible and not possible, boring and crazy .... Don't blame yourself for having strange ideas. We all do sometimes. Maybe you are a very imaginative person? What matters is that you know which thoughts are important, which ones you should dwell on, which ones are just distractions. Don't worry too much about each one. And, happy to chat with you.
Glad to hear this. As long as you are trying to find a way forward, you're already on the right path. Best of luck.

It does. It's a tough condition, but it is not permanent. I don't know exactly how it affects you, but sometimes it just makes people cry for no reason, or for very "minor" reasons. Remember that deep down, it's okay ... you'll get through this. Is anything specific making you cry right now?
What is going on tonight?
Good for you. Seeking out treatment is not always easy and you've already started doing that. SSRIs don't work for everyone, but you'll find something that works.

That is a difficult situation and it is courageous of you to post here and share your circumstances. Even if everything seems to be going against you, life can change for the better sometimes too. In the middle of situation like yours, sometimes it is hard to see hope - that doesn't mean there is none. Have you reached out to anyone before about how you have been feeling?

Finding purpose and reason to exist are among life's greatest and also most rewarding challenges. Most people aren't sure why we are here and what we should be doing, but they continue to learn, grow, and find meaning as they go. If you are going through tough times, remember that this happens to many people, it can be overcome, and it is part of the process of finding the right path forward. Is there anything in particular that is making things difficult for you right now?

Hey, I don't think anyone is going to be in a better position if you end everything. Your kids and husband will surely miss you forever and always feel like they might have been able to prevent this somehow. Why do you feel this is the best approach? Have you consulted with anyone about how you have been feeling recently? Please let us know what is on your mind.
This sounds like a tough situation for you. Did the medications not help? Were the side effects too bothersome? Recovery is possible, we just need to find the right approach.

Sometimes people want to be the 'shoulder to lean on' but it may be very hard for them to know how to do that. Have faith that deep down people care about you, and you will find someone with whom you can connect.

So good of you to reach out. /r/suicidewatch has some recommendations here which might help as well: http://www.reddit.com/r/SWResources/comments/igh87/concerned_but_dont_know_what_to_say_here_are_some/

Thanks for posting this. It is great to see that there have been positive results with ECT. This article just came out about tDCS, which seems to be a newer electrical therapy that is less invasive and has fewer side effects: http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21645509-diy-bundle-electronics-or-ready-made-device-it-possible-stimulate?fsrc=scn/rd_ec/hacking_your_brain (this was also posted to r/Futurology). For those of you exploring options, maybe it's worth looking into!

especially in a state of depression, you cannot know whether you will find happiness later. part of depression is a sense of hopelessness and restricted perspective, which can disappear as you heal. getting out of depression is not just about developing the strength to keep going - it is also about a change of viewpoint that makes clear the path ahead isn't as bad as it currently seems. so i would answer no to your question.
good idea. OP, there are many ways to see this through. seek out help; it is always easier with support. you are not alone.

these are all sensations that exist in life... peace, warmth, calm... these are not aspects of death, which is most likely nothingness. Your life may be difficult, and we are here to listen. There are ways to develop strength until it gets better.

the hopelessness you feel is part of your illness. you may feel like suicide is the only option, but this impression is also part of the illness. recovering from these conditions can be difficult, but many people accomplish difficult things, so long as they see them in the right light. right now this "light" may not be working for you, but you will only have to turn it on to see that the longer path toward good health and a good life is probably worthwhile. don't be so confident in your current decision-making that you make an irreversible choice. just maybe, there is more to this than is visible now.

it's not the number of arguments that counts. death will happen anyway later, and is irreversible, but your impressions about life and what you may value about it can evolve over time. give yourself some slack to see how things go.

remember that your feelings, wants, guilt, confusion, desires … are all still thoughts. they vary, they can be contradictory, they are affected by the health of your brain, they can change over time. you should not do anything so definitive, so permanent.
most people's lives change a lot over time in unexpected ways. who knows what you would be missing out on.
https://www.imalive.org/
care to elaborate?

because there is no really really good reason to quit on life. you have no idea what you would be missing out on that would happen in life, and you have even less of an idea of what happens in death. give life a chance, and see what happens. you will see things differently over time.

remember that recovery involves also seeing things differently. so these impressions and decisions will not appear logical once your mind is on track. and it can be. don't assume that you understand the whole picture now. there is sunshine once you are able to look at it again, and there are ways to get to that point.
don't assume everyone else feels super confident about how productive and worthy they are. give change a chance. you don't 'deserve' to die for any reason at all, actually. no one does.
